name: MACRO (Museo d'Arte Contemporanea di Roma)
funding: €3.5M budget. Roma Capitale municipal cultural council and Azienda Speciale Palaexpo public agency.
watch: Reimagined under the 'Museum for Preventive Imagination' manifesto with 100% free admission and complete freedom from commercial sponsors.

name: Hayward Gallery (Southbank Centre)
funding: £38M Southbank Centre operating budget. Arts Council England National Portfolio Organisation (NPO), admissions, and Southbank Centre trust.
watch: Part of Europe largest arts center on London South Bank; severed commercial naming conflicts and adheres to statutory public arts charter.

name: BAK, basis voor actuele kunst
funding: Until 2024 the culture ministry (64 percent) and Utrecht (31 percent) paid 97 percent of EUR 1.98M income. Both ended multi-year funding from 2025; 2025 income fell to EUR 538k. Utrecht grants Basecamp EUR 62,500 a year for 2027 to 2028.
watch: Utrecht ended its multi-year subsidy from 2025 despite a positive advisory report, BAK says; the Council for Culture advised ending state funding. Four post-academic institutions wrote in support.
why_flagged: Until 2024 the culture ministry (64 percent) and Utrecht (31 percent) paid 97 percent of EUR 1.98M income. Both ended multi-year funding from 2025; 2025 income fell to EUR 538k. Utrecht grants Basecamp EUR 62,500 a year for 2027 to 2028.
records_note: Its ANBI page posts annual reports 2021 to 2025 with balance sheets, names seven funders in an undated list, and lists the supervisory board.

name: Casco Art Institute: Working for the Commons
funding: Structural support from Mondriaan Fund, City of Utrecht and Stichting DOEN via Arts Collaboratory.
watch: Pioneered the institutional shift from an exhibition showroom to a living commons and cooperative ecosystem. Led by Binna Choi, Casco restructured its entire internal governance according to feminist economics, mutual care, and collective unlearning.
records_note: Its Foundation page says annual and financial reports sit in a public Dropbox folder; the About page names three funders, the Team page the board.

name: Kunstinstituut Melly
funding: Income €2.7M (2025), €1.9M of it subsidy from Rotterdam and OCW. Ammodo, Niemeijer Fonds, Droom en Daad, Mondriaan Fonds, VSBfonds, ELJA, Elise Mathilde and Zabawas also give.
watch: Niemeijer Fonds was founded by a Groningen tobacco manufacturer's daughter. A 2017 open letter demanded the Witte de With name go; renamed 2021.
why_flagged: Income €2.7M (2025), €1.9M of it subsidy from Rotterdam and OCW. Ammodo, Niemeijer Fonds, Droom en Daad, Mondriaan Fonds, VSBfonds, ELJA, Elise Mathilde and Zabawas also give.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2020 to 2025, the 2025 accounts, a named supervisory board and a 2025 thank-you list of funders.

name: De Appel
funding: Mondriaan Fonds and Amsterdams Fonds voor de Kunst fund it for 2025 to 2028. Ammodo, the city's districts, Fonds voor Cultuurparticipatie and Cultuurfonds add project money.
watch: In 2015 the board dismissed director Lorenzo Benedetti; the Curatorial Programme tutors asked the board to resign and withdrew. An Amsterdam inquiry found the board fell short.
why_flagged: Mondriaan Fonds and Amsterdams Fonds voor de Kunst fund it for 2025 to 2028. Ammodo, the city's districts, Fonds voor Cultuurparticipatie and Cultuurfonds add project money.
records_note: De Appel posts annual reports for 2008 to 2025 with accounts, names its supervisory board, and names its funders in the 2025 report.

name: Framer Framed
funding: Ministry of OCW, Amsterdams Fonds voor de Kunst, Stadsdeel Oost and VriendenLoterij Fonds, per its about page.
watch: Decolonial art platform founded in 2009. The Rabo ArtLab project is in no source I opened.
records_note: Framer Framed names its six-member supervisory board and four public funders on undated pages, but posts no annual reports or accounts.

name: W139
funding: Public subsidies from Amsterdams Fonds voor de Kunst (AFK) and Mondriaan Fund, artist dues, and foundation grants. Zero commercial gallery representation.

name: Rijksakademie van beeldende kunsten
funding: About EUR 5.2M income in 2024, mostly Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science money, with Ammodo as main partner, plus Rabobank and De Nederlandsche Bank.
watch: Provides multi-year studio research for ~50 selected artists worldwide, accompanied by public open studios and public lecture programs. Main partner Ammodo (2022-26). Brouwerij 't IJ (alcohol) backs Open Studios. A Dec 2024 alumni campaign challenged its governance.
records_note: The Rijksakademie posts annual reports for 2015 to 2025, an ANBI form, a named supporter list and its four-member supervisory board.

name: Stroom Den Haag
funding: Municipality of The Hague cultural allocation, Mondriaan Fund, public research grants.

name: West Den Haag
funding: Mondriaan Fund, City of The Hague, non-profit cultural trusts. Fully audited accounts published annually.

name: Vleeshal Center for Contemporary Art
funding: City of Middelburg, Mondriaan Fund, Province of Zeeland. Complete public accounting under Dutch ANBI non-profit guidelines.
watch: The Province of Zeeland, named in the first draft, is not listed there.
records_note: Vleeshal posts annual reports and accounts for 2019 to 2025, names its supervisory board, and names its two public funders on an undated page.
